articles.headline: Crossplane 2.4.0 released: security fixes and a November 2026 EOL for legacy claims
articles.dek: Crossplane v2.4.0 ships its routine quarterly update, patches known security issues, and flags the end‑of‑life deadline for the current claim model.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Crossplane dropped v2.4.0 on Aug 20 2026, delivering the expected quarterly refresh plus a batch of security fixes and an EOL notice that will hit in November 2026 [FACT:9e768f21e51df0884cd80c4cbdd0c012][FACT:f3beb2a2207248acccacef49c1db9e80][FACT:f7d238535f3faf724707a6fd9e365983].
Why This Matters

If you run Kubernetes workloads with Crossplane, the security patches close known attack vectors, and the looming EOL means you’ll need to transition any legacy, cluster‑scoped claims before the deadline to stay supported [FACT:f3beb2a2207248acccacef49c1db9e80][FACT:0e6f20661859356e60a83957811b91a6].
What Happened

The release follows Crossplane’s regular quarterly cadence — a predictable cadence that the project uses for all major updates [FACT:9e768f21e51df0884cd80c4cbdd0c012]. It also bundles a set of security fixes into the toolchain and publicly marks this version as the last supported release before the November 2026 EOL [FACT:f3beb2a2207248acccacef49c1db9e80][FACT:666bb683279cd37c49b82112de78ba65].
Builder View

Upgrade to 2.4.0 without a migration plan; the upgrade path is built‑in and does not require moving resources to a new schema [FACT:6f01a933bf40ac95228f5a24cdda3859]. After you upgrade, start planning to retire legacy cluster‑scoped claims before the November 2026 cutoff to avoid losing critical fixes later [FACT:0e6f20661859356e60a83957811b91a6][FACT:666bb683279cd37c49b82112de78ba65].
Open Questions
The EOL notice applies only to this release, leaving the exact schedule for post‑EOL critical patches unclear [FACT:f7d238535f3faf724707a6fd9e365983].
Ardur Take

Crossplane 2.4.0 is a modest bump that matters: apply it now for the security patches, note the November 2026 EOL, and use the hassle‑free upgrade path to stay on the supported track [FACT:f3beb2a2207248acccacef49c1db9e80][FACT:6f01a933bf40ac95228f5a24cdda3859][FACT:f7d238535f3faf724707a6fd9e365983].

articles.headline: ChatGPT search now uses the site: operator at scale
articles.dek: Promptwatch reports that the built‑in web search behind ChatGPT now respects site: filters, letting builders narrow the source pool on the fly.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Promptwatch’s automated tracking shows ChatGPT’s search layer now applies the site: operator across the whole web [FACT:f4ee3ce00deeadf4eff6c01fe4189062][FACT:389a1e7516c782a584ef4346eb8a1ac2]. The shift appeared in the service’s logs by mid‑August and marks the first time the model enforces domain‑level constraints at scale [FACT:950cc61eabf19b1d38a2683bee597c10].
Why This Matters

Restricting results to a known domain cuts down on hallucinated facts and yields more reproducible citations—critical when you pipe ChatGPT’s answers into downstream pipelines [FACT:950cc61eabf19b1d38a2683bee597c10]. Promptwatch’s automation already collects response metrics, so the change is visible in real‑time analytics [FACT:7058589b6c0d28b0211de6ac7048bbee].
What Happened

On Aug 18, Promptwatch flagged that every search request with a site: prefix was being honoured by the model’s internal retriever [FACT:389a1e7516c782a584ef4346eb8a1ac2]. By Aug 20, Simon Willison’s Weblog confirmed the observation, citing Promptwatch’s own tracking data [FACT:f4ee3ce00deeadf4eff6c01fe4189062]. OpenAI’s public comment was limited to a vague statement on Aug 6, offering no technical clarification [FACT:304039ff0943f6be9027aaccae230758].
Builder View

If your app relies on ChatGPT‑generated URLs, expect those URLs to stay inside the domain you specify. You may need to tighten URL‑extraction patterns, but you can also lean on the tighter source pool for more deterministic downstream parsing [FACT:950cc61eabf19b1d38a2683bee597c10]. Reddit users have already started experimenting to confirm the new system prompt, indicating the community is actively probing the behavior [FACT:d6e3b38dcaddae9be1385060edcf1fe5].
Open Questions

OpenAI has not detailed whether the site: behaviour is configurable, how it affects latency, or if it could be rolled back in future updates [FACT:304039ff0943f6be9027aaccae230758][FACT:2965010438cc1782d72f2a9d4229be6e]. The signal comes from a single monitoring service, so developers should treat it as an early indicator rather than a hard‑coded contract [FACT:f4ee3ce00deeadf4eff6c01fe4189062].
Ardur Take

The observation is concrete (Promptwatch’s logs) but limited to one data source, so confidence in the fact‑of‑change is high while confidence in long‑term impact is medium. Watch for an official OpenAI statement before baking the behavior into production‑critical code [FACT:f4ee3ce00deeadf4eff6c01fe4189062].
